To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

lexicality effects in verbal short-term recognition tasks are strong, that they are not the exclusive product of redintegrative mechanisms, and that they are not necessarily the product of redintegrating mechanisms at all.
the lexicality effect observed in STM tasks is not due to reconstruction mechanisms but rather to the direct activation of lexicon-semantic knowledge during STM encoding and maintenance.
the lexicality effect is observed in the fast recognition task, which is a strong support for the direct activation of lexical representations in verbal short-term-memory tasks.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the role of long-term memory knowledge in verbal short-term recognition tasks.
the nature of memory processes involved in verbal short-term recognition memory, and the way these processes interact with long-term memory.
the role of semantic memory in short term verbal memory.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
lexicality effects in verbal STM tasks reflect a combination of direct and indirect lexical LTM effects.
the lexicality effect in STM is the product of a mixture of both direct and reconstructive LTM effects.
the redintegration account of the lexicality effect in STM is supported by the data but not the extreme version of the account.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
lexicality effect in STM is not a product of redintegration processes, but rather a product of direct access to semantic information.
redintegration is not necessary to explain the lexicality effect in STM recognition tasks.
the redintegration hypothesis is supported, but that it does not explain all the LTM effects observed in verbal STM tasks.
The main takeaway from our work is that

LTM effects in verbal STM tasks are not the result of reconstruction mechanisms, but are rather the result of the activation of lexical LTM representations in parallel with the activation of phonological traces.
the locus of lexicality effects in verbal STM remains unclear, and that more research is needed to clarify the role of lexical LTM in verbal STM.
